$schema: component-compatibility.schema (informal) — see COMPONENT_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX milestone report for classification rules

classificationLegend.A: FULL RUNTIME + INTERACTIVE — simulation mapping + compatible pins + runtime model + realtime input capability confirmed by RuntimeCapabilityResolver AND wired to ISimulationInputChannel
classificationLegend.B: RUNTIME OUTPUT — real runtime model exists (either runner), component reacts to program logic, no live user input
classificationLegend.C: WIRING VALIDATION — dedicated pin/wiring rule (Require() checks) exists, no runtime behavior in either runner
classificationLegend.D: VISUAL ONLY — renders on canvas; either only the generic structural-only wiring warning applies, or no SupportedPins entry exists at all
classificationLegend.E: IMPORTED / NOT MAPPED — present in Component Registry (Fritzing/KiCad import) but SimulationComponentType is null

visualCapabilityLegend.REAL_PROVIDER_VISUAL: Real, verified external visual asset depicting the actual physical component, with real pin geometry from that same source (today: exclusively @wokwi/elements — Fritzing/KiCad have never produced a usable visual asset, see REAL COMPONENT VISUAL milestone Checkpoint A). Independent of simulation/runtime status.
visualCapabilityLegend.VERIFIED_INTERNAL_VISUAL: A hand-built StemFlow illustration that has been checked against a real reference (photo/datasheet) for shape, connector grouping, and pin placement — not photorealistic, but not a meaningless placeholder either. Added in the VISUAL REFINEMENT / EXPANSION phase: most of these SVGs already existed and were already reference-accurate, they had just never been formally assessed against the matrix.
visualCapabilityLegend.GENERIC_FALLBACK: A clean, honestly-generic card/shape — never claims to depict the real physical component. Pin NAMES may still be verified (see pinDefinitionVerified) even when the visual itself is generic.

components.reason: CORRECTED (was 'No runtime model in either runner' — false, see below). A real scripted-sensor runtime model DOES exist in source for QEMU: SensorRuntimeHeaderGenerator.cs (Dht22Type/Dht11Type) reads sensorScenario timeline from diagram JSON and generates a StemFlowDHT C++ class (readTemperature/readHumidity, step-function lookup by millis()), injected into the compiled firmware by FirmwareCacheService (gated by SimulationRunner:Qemu:EnableSensorInputScenario=true in appsettings.json). Live-verified via real Docker/arduino-cli compile this milestone: the generated class text itself compiles successfully (confirmed 'Compile OK'). HOWEVER the documented/shipped contract is currently BROKEN — the sample exercise (virtualLabSampleExercises.ts, Bai 10) and the generator's own code comment both require student code to write '#include "StemFlowDHT.h"', but no such file is ever written into the compile sandbox (SimulationCompileService writes only sketch.ino) — live-verified compile failure: 'fatal error: StemFlowDHT.h: No such file or directory'. Net result: no WORKING end-to-end runtime today for code written the documented way, so classification stays C — but the correct reason is 'blocked by a real, narrow compile-contract bug', not 'no runtime model'. Not fixed this milestone (STEP 14: do not touch the generator unless necessary) — flagged as a follow-up bug.
missingRequirements: fix: write a StemFlowDHT.h stub into the sketch sandbox (or drop the #include requirement from the documented contract) so the already-correct generated class actually compiles for code following the sample exercise

components.reason: Component Source Resolution milestone. Identity confirmed as the standard YL-69 probe + LM393 comparator driver-board module (VCC/GND/DO/AO), not a raw 2-prong probe alone — matches StemFlow's existing pin declaration. Sources checked: @wokwi/elements (no soil-moisture element exists), Fritzing core (SparkFun_Soil_Moisture_Sensor.fzp is a DIFFERENT 3-pin VCC/GND/SIG analog-only breakout, wrong identity; ChirpSoilMoistureSensor.fzp is a different I2C/SPI capacitive sensor, wrong identity — both rejected, not just accepted for being 'close enough'), KiCad core (Sensor_Humidity library has no assembled-module symbol). Pin SEMANTICS verified via cross-corroborated vendor documentation (e.g. electropeak.com/soil-moisture-sensor-1) describing the same standard VCC/GND/DO/AO convention — no single official manufacturer for this generic/commodity module, but the convention is consistent everywhere it's documented. Added the dedicated wiring rule this milestone (a wiring rule only needs pin semantics, not geometry) moving this from D to C. REAL COMPONENT VISUAL Phase 2: re-assessed the existing fallback-card SVG against the real YL-69 module — 2 metal probes at the top + a separate comparator board below matches the real 2-piece design exactly; all 4 pin y-coordinates sit consistently at the card's mid-height. Upgraded to VERIFIED_INTERNAL_VISUAL — this was never actually a missing-asset problem, just an unassessed existing one.
